title: Positional Escape Basics
description: Core escapes for the three positions beginners get stuck in most: side control, mount, and the back.

media.title: 3 MUST-KNOW Side Control Escapes (Lachlan Giles)
notes: Context: Lachlan presents three major side-control escape paths and explains when each becomes appropriate based on distance, frames, and the opponent's base.
- [00:00-00:32] Main branches: frame to guard recovery, underhook to wrestle up, or sit-up escape to outside control.
- [01:23-03:20] Build distance with forearm frames, stiff-arm frames, shin/knee frames, and by turning onto your side.
- [01:23-02:24] Forearm frames redirect head/shoulder pressure; shin frames stretch the hips away and create space for the top leg.
- [05:26-07:19] If frames stall, swim for your own underhook, use pillow defense to beat the crossface, hip away, and reach for a leg.
- [07:19-09:29] If they switch their base to stop your knee coming through, block the bottom hip, clear the crossface, stiff-arm, and build up.

media.title: How I Escape EVERYONES Mount
notes: Context: this video teaches a kipping mount escape sequence. The main point is that the kip only works after you win inside position and displace their base.
- [00:06-00:26] Run the escape in order: inside position first, base displacement second, kip last.
- [00:26-00:51] Inside position has three parts: inside elbows, inside feet or knees, and inside forehead.
- [00:55-01:51] Control the hips with hands or frames, move your forehead inside, separate their feet, and avoid reaching your arms out where they can isolate you.
- [02:47-04:02] Before kipping, bridge to displace their base so their hips are no longer parallel to the mat and their weight is loaded over one knee.
- [04:14-05:43] Keep knees and feet together during the kip. The kip is extra disruption after their mount is already displaced, not the main force.

media.title: The ONLY Back Escape You Need (It's Simple)
notes: Context: this video studies Mason Fowler's back escape, especially escaping toward the choking-arm side in no-gi rather than defaulting to the control side.
- [02:53-07:17] Get to the choking side, then misalign your hips so your hips face a different direction than the attacker's hips.
- [10:07-11:13] Keep attention on the seatbelt instead of getting distracted by the hooks first.
- [11:13-12:52] Use a hook grip under the fingers to break the seatbelt, separate the hands, then quickly go two-on-one and remove the arm over your head.
- [13:43-15:15] After the shoulders reach the mat and you turn to face, use inside elbow/leg control or the crossed-feet follow-up to avoid simply giving up mount.

media.title: Kenta Iwamoto: How to Escape the Body Triangle in BJJ (Simple Hip Shift & Side Switch Trick!)
notes: Context: this short body-triangle clip focuses on shifting the pelvis inside the lock, then changing sides without letting the top player mount.
- [00:00-00:18] Shift your pelvis/hips inside the body triangle to make the lock harder to keep.
- [00:22-00:38] When switching sides, overwrap and hold the opponent's leg instead of just rolling across.
- [00:38-00:55] Put weight through their leg and pin the knee to the floor so they cannot easily extract it and mount.
- [00:49-01:00] Keep your head away, frame if they try to come up, and look to turn once the knee is controlled.

media.title: The Best Way To Escape From The Jiu Jitsu Body Triangle by Gordon Ryan
notes: Context: Gordon frames body-triangle escapes around upper-body side and leg-lock configuration, then demonstrates an overhook-side, top-side triangle escape.
- [01:41-02:35] Systematize body-triangle escapes by upper-body side and whether the triangle is locked on the top or bottom hip.
- [03:24-04:15] Keep the primary defensive hand in place with inside thumb position so the choking hand stays controlled.
- [04:16-04:56] Use the secondary hand as a hand assist instead of relying on foot-lock counters.
- [04:58-06:14] Put the secondary elbow under the opponent's knee, rotate/turn down to expose the ankle, then scissor your legs to trap that leg.
- [06:14-08:18] Once the triangle starts to unravel, control the foot, square your hips up if they try to relock, clear the bottom hook, and then deal with the upper body.
